We deliver dealership-standard diagnostics, mechanical repairs, auto electrical work, air conditioning services and logbook servicing using advanced diagnostic equipment and high-grade parts. Our reputation is built on honest diagnosis, transparent upfront pricing, quality workmanship and a 24-month/20,000 km warranty. We value precision, clear communication and genuine customer care in a professional, well-equipped workshop environment that prioritises accuracy over shortcuts.
About the Position:
The Automotive Technician (Motor Mechanic) is responsible for diagnosing, maintaining and repairing Mercedes-Benz and European vehicles to a high technical standard. This hands-on role is central to delivering reliable, dealership-level service without the dealership price tag, ensuring vehicles leave the workshop performing safely and smoothly while supporting the growth of a specialist independent business.
Key Responsibilities:
Diagnose mechanical and electrical faults using advanced diagnostic equipment (including Xentry/ISTA and similar systems) and interpret live data and fault codes accurately.
Perform scheduled logbook servicing and routine maintenance to manufacturer specifications.
Repair and replace components including engines, transmissions, braking systems, steering, suspension, cooling systems, clutches and related mechanical assemblies.
Carry out auto electrical repairs, battery/charging system diagnostics, and air conditioning inspections, leak testing and re-gassing.
Dismantle, inspect, repair or replace worn or defective parts and reassemble components to correct specifications, referring to service manuals and technical data.
Road-test vehicles where required and verify repairs meet performance and safety standards.
Maintain a clean, organised and safe workshop environment, complete job cards accurately and communicate findings clearly to the business owner/customers.
Source and fit OEM or equivalent high-grade parts and support transparent quoting processes.
Requirements:
Australian citizens and permanent residents are encouraged to apply.
Certificate III in Automotive Technology, Certificate III in Light Vehicle Mechanical Technology, or an equivalent recognised qualification.
Minimum 4 years’ experience as a qualified Automotive Technician / Motor Mechanic.
Strong technical skills in diagnosing and repairing modern European vehicles, including familiarity with electronic control systems and diagnostic software.
Excellent attention to detail, problem-solving ability, clear communication skills and a professional, customer-focused approach.
Ability to work independently, follow manufacturer procedures, and maintain high standards of workmanship and workshop safety.
How to Apply:
To apply, applicants must submit their resume with a valid email address through this online portal.
Only shortlisted candidates will be contacted.

Primary coordinator for various aspects of new energy processes   Your new company     At Hays, we believe in being long-term partners with our people, as well as our customers. Together, we will work for your tomorrow, and the possibilities are endless.  With over 50 years of business success, we have built a reputation as the world leader in specialist recruitment and workforce solutions. Joining Hays isn't just being part of a global business leader; we're also the industry leading recruiting experts in Australia. We offer our people a career like no other.      Your new role     We are seeking a New Energy Information Management & Operations Analyst to join the Hays team based in our Melbourne office. This is a full time permanent role commencing immediately. The salary is $95,400 + Super.   Responsibilities   
 
 Coordinate renewable energy installations and project delivery activities.   
 Manage schedules, work orders, network applications and project documentation.   
 Act as the key contact between customers, contractors and internal teams.   
 Support supply chain and logistics to ensure projects are delivered on time.   
 Analyse operational data and provide insights to improve performance.   
 Drive process improvements and enhance operational efficiency.   What you'll need to succeed     
 5+ years' experience in scheduling, coordination or field operations.   
 Background in energy, renewables, construction or a related industry.   
 Strong stakeholder management skills, particularly with contractors and trades.   
 Experience managing high-volume, multi-stage projects.   
 Strong analytical, problem-solving and organisational skills.   
 Excellent communication skills with a continuous improvement mindset     
 
  What you need to do now     If you're thinking of a new tomorrow for your career, let's work together to create it.  Contact Sandy Luhr, Senior Talent Acquisition Partner by submitting your application via the Apply Now button.  By joining Hays, you'll be part of an inclusive culture that celebrates diversity. We invite people of all genders, ages, cultures, abilities, backgrounds, and experiences to apply. This includes Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander peoples, people who belong to LGBTQIA+ community, neurodiverse individuals, and people with disabilities. If you require support and/or adjustments throughout our recruitment process please contact recruitment.anz@hays.com.au       Please  click here  to apply.
